title: A home for the whole process
summary: Bringing my projects and the thinking behind them into one place.
body: I want this site to be a clear picture of what I make, what I’m exploring, and how my ideas develop. That means making the full project collection easier to browse, alongside the more detailed case studies.
Updates is where I’ll share check-ins, progress, interests, and notes on why I’m pursuing an idea. The work includes finished builds and prototypes; their stages stay visible so the context is clear.
I’m also putting more care into how I present public code: useful documentation, clear credit, and a separation between personal working notes and material intended to be shared.

title: A new visual direction for the portfolio
summary: A quieter palette, moving wireframes, and a more visual way to explore the work.
body: The portfolio moved to a monochrome visual direction inspired by Louis Raillé’s site: condensed display typography, fine grids, and a dimensional gallery.

The implementation uses original animated terrain and screenshots from my own projects. The gallery supports keyboard navigation and touch; motion can be paused, and the site respects reduced-motion preferences.
The aim is to give the work room to speak while keeping case studies, project stages, and my résumé easy to reach.
